method: Snell's law in a stratified, windless atmosphere: a ray's horizontal trace speed c/cos(psi) is conserved; for flight-path angle gamma (climb > 0) the Mach-cone condition V.n = c_a gives cos(gamma)cos(psi)cos(phi) - sin(gamma)sin(psi) = 1/M at the aircraft; the leg is boomless if the largest trace speed over ray azimuths phi in [-60, 60] deg stays below the largest effective sound speed under the aircraft. Under-track closed form: M(gamma) = 1/cos(acos(1/Mcut) + gamma). Table: highest boomless Mach at flight-path angle gamma for a column whose level-flight cutoff is Mcut.
